title: San Diego FC defeats San Jose Earthquakes in battle for playoff spot
seoTitle: San Diego FC Beats San Jose Earthquakes in Playoff Race
subtitle: The matchup decides whether the San Diego team maintains the final Western Conference playoff spot
excerpt: On Saturday, San Diego FC and San Jose Earthquakes faced off in a decisive MLS match, where the result could determine San Diego's postseason survival.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
On Saturday, San Diego FC and San Jose Earthquakes faced off in a decisive MLS match, where the result could determine the San Diego club's survival in the final stage of the championship.

San Diego tries to secure the final playoff spot

With 30 points, San Diego FC is just one point ahead of three teams in the Western Conference, putting them in the final playoff position. The match against the San Jose Earthquakes, scheduled for 7:30 PM on Wednesday, September 9, was viewed as an internal final, as any dropped points could knock the San Diego team out of the standings.

Recent performance of both teams

San Diego FC won three consecutive home matches but suffered a 1-0 defeat against Orlando City in their last away game. In their previous matchup, the San Jose Earthquakes drew 1-1 with Austin FC, with Beau Leroux scoring for the San Jose side. San Diego FC's defeat against Orlando City brought the team back within reach of their pursuers, while the San Jose Earthquakes remain winless in five consecutive road games.

Statistics influencing the matchup

Data shows that San Diego FC averages 53.5% possession and 4.8 corners per match, while the San Jose Earthquakes record 51.5% possession and 5.6 corners. San Diego FC averages 1.5 goals per game, with 3.9 shots on target and 12.2 total attempts, while the San Jose Earthquakes record 1.1 goals per game, with 12.3 attempts and 4.5 shots on target. San Diego FC's top scorers are Elias Achouri, Amahl Pellegrino, Gabriel Pirani, Anders Dreyer, and Marcus Ingvartsen, each with two goals. The team's leading assist provider is Anders Dreyer, with four assists.

Confirmed lineups and formations

For San Diego FC, the confirmed 4-3-3 lineup includes Carlos Dos Santos (goalkeeper), Oscar Verhoeven, Manu Duah, Christopher McVey, Dagur Dan Thorhallsson, Anibal Godoy, Jeppe Tverskov, Gabriel Pirani, Anders Dreyer, Onni Valakari, and Elias Achouri. Meanwhile, the San Jose Earthquakes, playing in a 3-5-2 formation, featured Angus Gunn (goalkeeper), Daniel Munie, David Romney, Reid Roberts, Niko Tsakiris, Ian Harkes, Jack Jasinski, Beau Leroux, Vitor Costa, Luka Jovanovic, and Preston Judd.

Betting expectations and odds

Bookmakers list San Diego FC as the favorite with odds of -137, indicating a 57.8% probability of victory. The San Jose Earthquakes have odds of +295, suggesting lower chances of success. Additionally, there are betting options for goals, corners, and player performances, such as Onni Valakari's odds to score at least one goal in the match.

Conclusion

The game between San Diego FC and the San Jose Earthquakes represents a critical juncture for both teams. While San Diego FC fights to maintain the final playoff spot, the San Jose Earthquakes look to overcome their negative road streak. The outcome will determine who advances in the competition and who remains in the hunt for an MLS title.

With information from Sportsgambler, Field Level Media.
